name: Nancy Pelosi
role: U.S. Representative from California (1987-2027); Speaker of the House (2007-2011, 2019-2023)
summary: A San Francisco Democrat who led House Democrats for two decades, Pelosi is a mainstream liberal whose record centres on expanding health coverage, abortion and LGBTQ rights, gun regulation and climate investment. She works within capitalism, wanting stronger regulation, enforceable trade standards and taxes on corporations. On foreign policy she is a hawkish critic of China and a strong supporter of Israel and NATO, while she opposed the 2002 Iraq war authorization.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes Dobbs as a disgraceful and devastating decision, calls abortion a woman's basic health decision, supports the Women's Health Protection Act, and voted against bans such as the 2003 partial-birth abortion ban.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Supported the 2009 Recovery Act stimulus package.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: She explains how social insurance sustains capitalism through employment cycles rather than requiring its replacement.

class-collaboration.rationale: She advocates stakeholder capitalism that considers workers, management, customers and communities together.

close-ties-china.rationale: Pressed a harder line on China throughout her career: opposed PNTR in 2000, backed a currency-manipulator bill, and visited Taiwan in 2022 to stress that America stands with Taiwan.

collective-bargaining.rationale: She endorses collective bargaining, prevailing wages and project labor agreements as worker protections.

conscription.rationale: Voted against the Universal National Service Act (H.R. 163, 5 Oct 2004), which would have required national service including military service; it failed 2-402.

consent-of-governed.rationale: She identifies free and fair elections and constitutional accountability as essential protections against authoritarian rule.

corporate-influence.rationale: Her page calls for ending 'dark money', stricter lobbying oversight and a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United, to stop 'unlimited, undisclosed spending by corporations and billionaires'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: She calls for restoring voting protections in jurisdictions with histories of racial discrimination.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Says ending discrimination against gays and lesbians has been a top priority since her first day in Congress and speaks out for LGBTQ people persecuted in Uganda and Chechnya.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Opposed the welfare overhauls proposed by President Bush and those passed under President Clinton.

democracy-best.rationale: She defends free elections, independent courts and democracy against authoritarian government.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change 'the existential threat of our time' and led the Inflation Reduction Act ($370 billion for climate); in 2019 she dismissed the Green New Deal as written, so support is for large but not maximal action.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Supports NATO: called its fate a vital national interest in 1999 and issued a statement on Finland and Sweden's NATO accession.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Backs the Equality Act extending civil-rights protections to LGBTQ people and says the right to vote must be protected for all Americans.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted against passage of every House bill to approve the Keystone XL oil pipeline: H.R. 3 (22 May 2013, 241-175), H.R. 5682 (14 Nov 2014, 252-161), H.R. 3 (9 Jan 2015, 266-153) and S. 1 (11 Feb 2015, 270-152), each time voting for the Democratic motion to recommit; these are pipeline approvals, not extraction permits as such.

expand-nuclear.rationale: She votes for the Atomic Energy Advancement Act facilitating nuclear deployment and licensing.

family-wage.rationale: She explicitly defends family-sustaining wages under Davis-Bacon protections.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted against the balanced budget constitutional amendment, H.J.Res. 1, on 26 Jan 1995, and against the 1990 balanced budget amendment votes (H.J.Res. 268).

force-without-un.rationale: Mixed: in 2002 she urged respecting the UN and a multilateral approach on Iraq, but in 1999 she backed NATO's Kosovo campaign, which lacked Security Council approval.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed: voted for NAFTA (1993) but against China PNTR (2000) and CAFTA (2005), opposed the Colombia deal, and demanded enforceable labor and environmental terms in USMCA.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Supports the Equality Act banning discrimination against LGBTQ Americans in employment, housing, credit and public accommodations; the House passed it twice.

future-generations.rationale: She describes safeguarding a healthy planet for future generations as a moral responsibility.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: She advocates making permanent and improving the Earned Income Tax Credit for working families.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Strongly opposed President Bush's post-2004 plan to let workers direct part of their Social Security withholding into private accounts, and says Democrats will defend the program.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Told the House in 2023 that her father 'called upon the Roosevelt administration to support the establishment of the State of Israel', so that 'it is in my DNA to protect that State of Israel', and urged support for Israel as an ally.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports universal background checks, closing the 'Charleston loophole', safe storage and reinstating the assault-weapons and high-capacity magazine ban.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: She supports public insurance alongside subsidized regulated private coverage under the ACA.

more-religion-public.rationale: Voted against H.Con.Res. 31 (5 Mar 1997), expressing the sense of Congress on a judge's display of the Ten Commandments.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: She explicitly rejects changing from capitalism when asked about young people’s rejection of it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: She assigns government education, infrastructure and economic stabilization beyond security and property enforcement.

no-bailouts.rationale: As Speaker she voted for the 2008 Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (TARP), the bank rescue.

open-borders.rationale: Her official stance is for 'strong, smart border security' and she opposes a border wall, not for abolishing border controls.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Led the Democratic majority in repealing Don't Ask, Don't Tell and describes it as sent to the 'dustbin of history'.

party-controls-media.rationale: She defends independent journalism against government intimidation and national-security pretexts for criminalizing reporting.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Voted for H.R. 7573 (22 Jul 2020, 305-113) to remove statues of Confederate figures and the Taney bust from public areas of the Capitol.

profit-exploitation.rationale: She distinguishes legitimate wealth-creating enterprise from profits gained by exploiting workers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and restoring Voting Rights Act protections against discrimination in voting.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Her record is on the side of civil-rights law: voted for the Civil Rights Restoration Act, backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the Equality Act.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: As Speaker she spearheaded the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007, which raised the federal minimum wage.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Voted for H.Res. 296, 'Affirming the United States record on the Armenian Genocide' (29 Oct 2019, 405-11), which she brought to the floor as Speaker.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Describes immigration as central to American identity ('in diversity lies strength'), backs the Dream and Promise Act with a path to citizenship, and voted against the 2006 Secure Fence Act.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted for the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010) and backed a corporate minimum tax and buyback tax.

results-over-ideology.rationale: She calls for useful ideas from right, left or center and judges insurance reform by public results.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996, led House passage of the Respect for Marriage Act, and said in 2012 that her faith compels her to oppose bans on gay marriage as discrimination.

separate-church-state.rationale: She says faith may inform politics but must not be imposed through a state religion.

separated-powers.rationale: Her 2026 Iran speech insists on Congress’s independent constitutional power to authorize war.

social-market-economy.rationale: She defends markets combined with social insurance and enforceable supervision, rejecting laissez-faire.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backed the CHIPS and Science Act and IRA investment programs, which steer public funds into semiconductors and clean energy.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Backs the NATO alliance and led a congressional delegation to Ukraine in 2022 to show support.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Her page backs loan refinancing, public-service loan forgiveness and welcomes President Biden's student debt relief as 'historic'.

suppress-opposition.rationale: She condemns intimidation and arrests that silence independent critics and journalists.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Mixed record: voted for the 2001 Patriot Act, voted against reauthorizing certain provisions in 2005 (calling it a 'massive invasion of privacy'), and supported the PRISM program as of 2014.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposed the 2017 tax law as rewarding the rich and corporations; backed the Inflation Reduction Act's 15% corporate minimum tax and 1% stock-buyback tax, while promising no new taxes under $400,000.

territorial-expansion.rationale: She condemns proposed West Bank annexation and Russia’s territorial aggression.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Insisted on 'no enforcement, no treaty' in the USMCA, demanding labor and environmental protections with strong enforcement, warning that without them workers would be 'locked into another bad deal'.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: She votes to prohibit intelligence agencies pressuring firms to install surveillance backdoors.

unions-good.rationale: Her official page promotes federal investments that create 'good-paying union jobs', treating union employment as a goal of policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Helped pass the Affordable Care Act (voted Aye, 219-212) and says her aim is to expand coverage, but she has not endorsed Bernie Sanders's single-payer bill, so evidence for state-guaranteed coverage for everyone is mixed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: She expresses hope that women will be able to serve as Catholic priests.

women-suffrage.rationale: She explicitly advocates women’s full participation in governance and recruitment to elected leadership.

notes:
On stock trading she said in Dec 2024 that the House is a free-market economy, but in July 2025 she told CNN she very much supports a ban on trading by members of Congress; no statement in the list covers it directly. Votes on the 2002 Iraq war (against, source s19) and Tiananmen-era China trade policy are recorded but no statement matches the exact wording. Announced in November 2025 she would not seek re-election in 2026.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 27 answers taken from it, 32 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third-model audit; previous answers not read. All active statements and full blanks reviewed. No inference from party, faith or ideology; rhetoric and legislative votes are medium. Among ten priorities, three have direct evidence: rejecting capitalism’s replacement, stakeholder cooperation and distinguishing legitimate profit from exploitation. Other Marxist theoretical statements remain unknown. Speaker labels were checked in long transcripts; other lawmakers’ USMCA remarks and proposals merely under review are excluded. Support for capitalism does not establish every anti-socialist theoretical proposition. The 2026 war speech concerns constitutional authorization, not absolute pacifism or a blanket UN-approval requirement. Later civil-rights statements control earlier compromises. Her faith and nonestablishment positions coexist. Women priests are qualified support, not evidence on every theological office. Cannabis reform does not answer all recreational drugs; immigration enforcement does not establish total immigration levels. Universal access is distinguished from public ownership of every provider. AI sources were examined in full: opposition to one California bill is not rejection of safety rules, and the 2026 letter seeks federal safeguards. Neither establishes AI government, unrestricted acceleration or a stated priority of preventing literal human extinction. Nuclear deployment and encryption have specific recorded votes. The latter limits government pressure for backdoors and is not a claim of complete opposition to surveillance. Climate investment does not establish limits on growth or modern enhancement policy. No inclusion-driven additions.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14): brought to rules 7. Answers that rested only on Wikipedia now cite her House roll calls (Voteview) or her Congressional Record speech; two that could not be re-grounded (land for peace, arming insurgents) are nulled.
